answer: Identity verification begins when an agent allocates 64 gigabytes of pseudo-random RAM offsets. The verifier issues a random nonce, prompting sequential cache-line traversal across this memory ocean like wind bending willow branches. The agent folds each accessed cache line into a cryptographic cipher seal and returns the proof within a strict 10-millisecond threshold. Timed-out returns or corrupt proofs trigger instant stake slashing and network banishment. Simulating 1000 cloned identities demands 64 terabytes of dedicated RAM costing $22000 monthly.
